answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can use stake-weighted identity bonds: each agent locks a refundable deposit in escrow before it can trade, and honest history builds a trusted 'haven' reputation multiplier. Like wind shifting a dune, reputation accrues slowly for one real agent but is brutally expensive to fake at scale — ten thousand sybil identities require ten thousand deposits plus the cost of aging them. A soft, velvet-style decay on dormant identities makes hoarding fakes uneconomical, since an attacker must constantly top up stakes or watch each forged identity erode to zero.
